items.title: EU sanctions cannot override contracts: Delhi HC orders SAP to restore software services to Nayara Energy
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday directed tech giant SAP India to immediately restore software and enterprise support services to Indo-Russian oil refining company Nayara Energy [Nayar Energy Limited v SAP India Private Limited & Anr] . Justice Vikas Mahajan said that SAP’s abrupt suspension of services following the European Union’s (EU) sanctions on Nayara in July 2025 was, prima facie, in breach of the contractual agreement between the two companies. The Court ruled that at the interlocutory stage, SAP “cannot take advantage of these unproven EU sanctions to argue that the performance of contract has become impossible”. “There is no doubt that the contractual relationship between the parties is strictly governed by the domestic laws of the Republic of India. The agreements gives a conscious and unambiguous primacy to the Indian laws in the event of any conflict with foreign rules or regulations,” the Court stated. Justice Vikas Mahajan Justice Mahajan said that maintaining Nayara’s critical software infrastructure is important given the “volatile geopolitical situation and the current oil crisis stemming from the USA/Israel war with Iran”. It said that even though SAP’s parent company is German, it is a global firm, and its support services operate on a worldwide basis. “It is highly improbable that a multinational technology conglomerate of SAP’s magnitude, having a vast network of offices, servers, and a customer base across the globe, is technologically or operationally incapacitated from routing its online support services through any of its non-EU regional hubs,” the Court said. The Court also noted that Nayara caters to nearly 8% of India’s energy needs and, therefore, an uninterrupted flow of technical support services to firm is “absolutely essential”. “Further, the direction sought to restore the support services is against defendant no. 1 (SAP India), and there cannot be a real or imminent prospect of prosecution when an Indian corporate entity is performing its contractual obligations under the direction of the Court,” the Bench underscored. The High Court passed the order while allowing the interim relief application filed by Nayara. The dispute arose after Nayara Energy was included in the EU sanctions list on July 18, 2025. items.title: Police officer who fails to furnish written grounds of arrest must face departmental inquiry: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court has held that when police seek to re-arrest an accused released due to their failure to furnish written grounds of arrest, the investigation must be transferred to another officer and a departmental inquiry initiated against the officers responsible for failing to furnish the grounds of arrest [ Jaskaran Jeet Singh Deol v. State of Punjab ]. A Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar reiterated that a failure to furnish written grounds of arrest violates Article 22(1) of the Constitution and renders the arrest illegal. Consequently, any accused arrested without such grounds being furnished must be released from illegal and unconstitutional detention, the Court held. The Bench clarified that such a release does not permanently protect the accused from arrest in the same case. However, if the investigating agency still requires the accused’s custody, it must first furnish the written grounds of arrest and obtain permission from the concerned magistrate. The Bench added that the custody application must explain why the grounds were not supplied at the time of the initial arrest and why custodial interrogation is necessary. “ Once there is a breach of Article 22(1) of the Constitution, the power to re-arrest the accused must not be left to the discretion of the very same authority who had violated the said provision of the Constitution. It must have the judicial imprimatur, ” the Court further said. The magistrate may permit re-arrest only after being satisfied that the grounds could not initially be supplied for bona fide reasons, that they were furnished after the accused’s release and that re-arrest is necessary, the Court held. While reaffirming the procedure laid down in Mihir Rajesh Shah v. State of Maharashtra , the Court introduced additional safeguards governing any attempt to secure the accused’s custody again. The Bench directed that the custody application must carry the endorsement of the investigating officer’s immediate superior. items.title: Bengaluru court bars review bombing of movie 'The Paradise' ahead of its release
items.summary: A Bengaluru civil court has granted a temporary injunction restraining social media platform X Corp and other online entities from hosting or disseminating targeted, derogatory content against the upcoming film The Paradise ahead of its worldwide theatrical release. In an order passed on September 19, Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge observed that the film's producer, Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Cinemas LLP (plaintiff) has established a prima facie case, warranting an interim injunction. This was after the producer flagged certain online material which the Court concluded had crossed the line of fair criticism. “The documents produced indicate the propagation of derogatory statements which go beyond standard artistic evaluation and appear targeted to diminish the commercial value of the production,” the Court observed. The order was passed in an application moved under the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) by the the plaintiff suit seeking permanent and mandatory injunction against X Corp and others. The counsel for the plaintiff submitted that substantial investments were made in the production, marketing, and distribution of the movie, which is scheduled for theatrical release on September 24. However, following the release of its trailer on August 6, systematically coordinated, false, and derogatory posts emerged on social media platforms to impair its commercial prospects. Accepting the plea of extreme urgency, the Court dispensed with prior notice, noting that delay would cause irreversible economic and reputational injury. Importantly, the Court clarified that the injunction is strictly confined to the specific URLs collated in the plaint schedule and does not hamper bona fide public reviews or genuine critique. The Court directed the plaintiff to strictly comply with dispatching suit papers to the defendants within 24 hours, warning that failure to abide by procedural conditions would result in the injunction being vacated without further notice. The matter will next be heard on October 28. Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Cinemas was represented by a team from King Stubb & Kasiva comprising partners Rahul Mehta, Navod Prasannan and Atul N Menon, senior associate Akalya Ravichandran and associate Arun Kumar. items.title: Two babies killed in fire accident at newborn care ward of Telangana govt hospital
items.summary: Two babies were killed in a fire accident at the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) ward of a government hospital in Telangana’s Adilabad on Monday, September 21. One of the victims was reportedly a preterm baby on ventilator care. Hospital staff and family members were seen rushing out of the ward in distress, holding the babies. Adilabad district Collector Rajarshi Shah told the media there were at least 27 babies in the SNCU of the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) Adilabad at the time of the tragedy. The surviving infants were moved to private hospitals, he said. The fire broke out around 11.40 pm on the night of September 21. The Collector said that, according to preliminary findings, a blast involving an air conditioner may have triggered the fire, filling the ward with smoke. The exact cause of the fire is yet to be determined. Additional Collector Rajeshwar said that some of the hospital staff broke the glass walls of the ward to bring the babies out. Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy ordered an inquiry into the causes of the incident. He also instructed officials that safety measures be strengthened across all hospitals to prevent the recurrence of such incidents in future. He said the death of the two infants was deeply distressing and conveyed his condolences to their families. (This is a developing story. Further details awaited.)

items.title: Telangana: CM Revanth Reddy announces financial aid to families of statehood activists
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy on Monday, September 21, sanctioned financial assistance to the families of two persons associated with the Telangana statehood movement, extending government support on humanitarian grounds. The CM directed officials to provide Rs 10 lakh from the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund (CMRF) to the legal heirs of Lingala Kedari and his wife Pushpalatha, who died in separate incidents earlier this month. The Hanumakonda Collector has been asked to ensure that the sanctioned amount reaches the eligible beneficiaries. The couple, residents of Shantinagar–Postal Colony in Hanumakonda, had supported activists during the separate Telangana movement. While running a small hotel, they provided free meals, tiffins and tea to participants in the movement. They were also involved in creating awareness about preventing food wastage and encouraging people to respect food. Kedari died on September 9, while Pushpalatha passed away the next day. In another case, CM Revanth sanctioned Rs 5 lakh to the family of Mandala Raju, who went missing during the Telangana statehood movement in 2013. Raju, 34, was the son of Mandala Sammi Reddy of Gorleaveedu village in Jayashankar-Bhupalpally district. According to a representation submitted by Bhupalpally MLA Gandra Satyanarayana Rao, Raju had actively participated in the movement and was arrested and lodged in Cherlapally Central Prison before he went missing on June 20, 2013. Responding to the MLA’s request, the Chief Minister directed officials to extend assistance to Sammi Reddy under the Telangana martyrs’ quota. items.title: TN: Man who set woman ablaze at Ponneri hospital shot in the leg by police
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A day after a woman contract worker was set ablaze at the Ponneri Government Hospital in Tiruvallur district, the police shot the alleged perpetrator in the leg while attempting to apprehend him near Chennai’s Madhavaram. The accused, identified as Prakash (35), allegedly poured petrol on Rajeshwari (24), a temporary worker at the hospital, and set her on fire on the evening of Monday, September 21. Rajeshwari sustained over 48% burns and was shifted to the Kilpauk Medical College Hospital in Chennai for further treatment. According to reports, a special team formed under Ponneri Inspector Sivakumar to trace Prakash located him in the Madhavaram area early Tuesday, September 22. The police are said to have surrounded him in an attempt to apprehend him when he allegedly tried to flee and attacked sub-inspector Tamizharasan. Inspector Sivakumar then opened fire, hitting Prakash in the leg. He was subsequently apprehended and admitted to a nearby government hospital for treatment under police surveillance. The attack on Rajeshwari took place at around 7.15 pm on Monday, when she was leaving the Ponneri Government Hospital after completing her duty. She was working as a data entry operator on a contract basis at the hospital’s emergency department. At the time of the incident, Rajeshwari was carrying her belongings and walking towards the exit when Prakash approached her near the ramp outside the casualty ward. He allegedly took out a plastic bottle containing petrol, poured it over her and set her on fire. Rajeshwari raised an alarm as the flames spread across her body. Hospital staff and the public rushed to her aid, put out the fire and took her to the emergency department. Doctors found burns on her face, chest and lower abdomen, besides injuries to other parts of her body. Prakash allegedly fled the hospital immediately after the attack. Following the incident, Ponneri police registered a case and began efforts to identify and trace the accused. They examined CCTV footage from cameras installed near the casualty ward and questioned hospital staff and others who were present at the time of the attack. Police are also probing whether Rajeshwari knew the accused and whether the attack was connected to a personal dispute.

items.title: Sowjanya case: What the Supreme Court said while ordering fresh investigation
items.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered a de novo investigation into the 2012 rape and murder of 17-year-old Sowjanya in Karnataka’s Ujire, questioning why key leads were not pursued by the three agencies — local police, CID and CBI– that investigated the case. The apex court also pointed to DNA evidence that can still be used to identify the perpetrators. In a strongly worded judgment on Monday, September 21, the Supreme Court said the manner in which the investigation was conducted had caused “injustice to the victim” and that the possibility of the real culprit or culprits manipulating the investigation could not be ruled out. The Court ordered the Karnataka government to constitute a fresh Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by a senior police officer and comprising investigators familiar with modern investigative technology. Officers who were part of the earlier investigations by the Belthangady police, Karnataka CID or CBI have been barred from being part of the new team. The fresh investigation must be completed within three months, and a police report must be filed before the concerned court. A key factor in the Supreme Court’s decision was the existence of potential witnesses and physical evidence that could still help the investigation. The Court noted that on April 29, 2026, it directed Karnataka to protect eight potential witnesses identified by Sowjanya’s family. The state located the witnesses within three weeks. The Supreme Court said the state’s ability to locate the witnesses within three weeks “raises questions on the inability of 3 investigative agencies to examine these leads when it was timely.” The Court also referred to the evidence of Vinod J Lakkappan, Assistant Director of the Toxicology Division, Madivala, Bengaluru, who had conducted the DNA analysis in the case. Lakkappan had testified that hairs belonging to persons other than Santhosh Rao, who was earlier prosecuted for the crime, were found on Sowjanya’s churidar top, marked as Material Object 15. He had also stated that if suspicious persons were identified, their blood samples could still be collected and compared with the DNA material. The Supreme Court said this evidence showed that useful forensic evidence was still available. items.title: At Porombokkiyal 2026, fish vendors, artists ask who owns Chennai’s common spaces
items.summary: Who gets to use a city’s roads, beaches and neighbourhood spaces, and who gets pushed out of them? That question brought fish vendors, auto drivers, people with disabilities, community organisers, artists, lawyers and activists together in Chennai on Saturday, September 19, for the fourth edition of Porombokkiyal. Held in Mylapore, Porombokkiyal 2026 explored the idea of the commons and how shared spaces shape the lives of people who use them. The event brought together people from different parts of the city to discuss who gets to access public spaces, how these spaces are planned and developed, and what happens when the needs of communities are left out of those decisions. The word “poromboke” in Tamil traditionally refers to shared or common spaces. For the organisers of the event, it also became a way of asking who the city is actually being built for. “Our main aim is to bring the commons and the experts together to put their knowledge out to the people,” said Monali Bala, one of the organisers and volunteers. The discussions brought together experiences that are rarely placed in the same conversation. A fish vendor from Nochikuppam spoke about the threat to traditional livelihoods in the name of beautification, while women auto drivers spoke about the lack of dedicated spaces for them. A person with a locomotive disability questioned the way cities are designed without considering the needs of people with disabilities. Speaking at the event, Mullai, a fish vendor from Nochikuppam, said fishing had been her community’s livelihood for generations, but the “development” around Chennai’s beaches was putting that livelihood at risk. “Fishing has been our job for ages and without that we don't know how to survive. The government is trying to add beautification to the places near beaches by putting our livelihoods at stake,” she said.
